messages:
Alex: FYI ran an overnight perf sweep against main on 8xT4, noticed PP bubble spiked ~2.5x after the new kernel selector roll
Priya: oh no. which selector landed? prefer-fused or the auto heuristic?
Alex: it flipped to selector v2 (auto-kernel-choice). quick trace summary:
```
model: redwood-medium
pp: 8
microbatches: 6
kernel_selector: v2-auto
kvcache_hit_rate: 47% (was 82% on canary)
pp_bubble_ms: baseline 13.2 -> 33.7
allreduce_tail_ms: 7.5 -> 15.1
overall_lat_p99: +22%
```
Tom: a ~35% drop in KV hit is massive. is the fused kernel changing layout/striding?
Alex: profiler shows the fused kernel produced a different KV memory layout. we're seeing many small DMA ops during KV lookup. flame graph points to waits around cudaMemcpyAsync at the start of windows
InfraBot: deploy:kernel-selector/v2-auto rolled at 02:18 UTC -> alert: pp_bubble_duration increased
Sandeep: can we hotfix by rolling back or pinning kernel choices per-model while we investigate?
Alex: rollback tested on a few hosts and latency returned to baseline. but pinning everywhere is a long-term burden
Lina: quick mitigation: increase microbatches 6 -> 10 to amplify compute overlap and amortize allreduce. tradeoff is higher per-sample latency but might reduce bubble ms
Priya: let's test that. also add a KV-prefetch flow: prefetch next-forward KV while current backward runs to cut sync points
Tom: experiment matrix I propose:
- selector: v1 vs v2
- microbatches: 4,6,8,10
- kv_prefetch: off/on
- comm_policy: async-allreduce vs sync
metrics: kvcache_hit, pp_bubble_ms, allreduce_tail_ms, p99
Alex: kicked off runs on staging. note: kv_prefetch needs adaptive window size to avoid OOMs (can't double-alloc KV buffers)
Sandeep: also check batching heuristic. sometimes we create skewed seq-length groups which make the selector oscillate mid-window
Priya: if the selector flips between microbatches it will thrash the KV cache. propose a selector-stability flag: freeze kernel per request-group/window
Lina: can we emit per-pp-window kernel+KV stats? current sampling is per-step and hides window transitions
Tom: I'll add a low-overhead `--pp-window-debug` to profiler that logs kernel id, kv_hits, compute_ms, comm_ms per window
Alex: sample failing run log snippet:
```
[window 12] kernelId: 0x3a pref_attn_fused
kv_hits: 12/32
compute_ms: 28.4
comm_ms: 18.7
note: 5 small cudaMemcpyAsync ops
```
Priya: if we detect >30% of KV ops as tiny DMAs fallback to kernel v1 for that model/seq combo
Sandeep: operationally, will pinning to v1 hurt other workloads? need a selector that is workload-aware and safe by default
Alex: agreed. tentative plan:
1) rollback kernel-selector to v1-auto on prod pools (Sandeep)
2) run the full experiment matrix with `--pp-window-debug` (Tom + Alex)
3) build `selector-stability` + `adaptive-kv-prefetch` prototype (Priya + Lina)
4) add CI perf gate: reject selector changes if kvcache_hit drops >15% or pp_bubble_ms increases >20% (Alex)
Lina: I'll open a draft PR for adaptive prefetch and add a telemetry schema for window-level stats
Tom: ETA for profiler flag and experiment harness: EOD tomorrow
Sandeep: initiating rollback on prod pool `pp-8-t4-a`, monitoring alerts
InfraBot: rollback:kernel-selector/v1-auto initiated by Sandeep at 08:43 UTC
Alex: after rollback early signals look back to normal. will paste experiment CSVs here when ready :thumbsup:
Priya: also add a unit test in selector that simulates KV fragmentation and asserts kernel-choice stability
Tom: will add test harness under runtime-kernel tests
Alex: keeping thread for updates. once experiments finish we'll converge on a selector that respects KV layout and batching heuristics
